item.title: A Festival of Bon-odori Dance and Japanese Street Food — Wed Sep 9, 2:00 PM — The Underground

The Japanese Language Circle also known as J-Circle, meets every Wednesday from 1:45 to 3:15 pm in Schmitt Hall room 125. item.title: Inner Body Meditation (20 Minutes) — Sat Sep 12, 10:45 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream "Awareness of the inner body takes you beyond the mind." - Eckhart Tolle
In this mediation session we will bring our attention here: to the inner body. Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. They will last around 20 minutes and cameras and microphones will be disabled.
(Depending on the situation, a free discussion may be held at the end with mics and cameras allowed.)
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys also organises a free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group. Visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/) for more information.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: The Sound of Harvest: Where East Meets West Through Music — Sun Sep 13, 3:00 PM — Memorial Auditorium at Montclair State University
item.description:
The Chinese Musicians Association of North America presents The Sound of Harvest, a concert bringing together musicians and instruments from a variety of cultural traditions. The program features Chinese instruments such as the erhu, pipa, guzheng, and ruan, alongside Japanese taiko and shinobue, African percussion, jazz piano, lute, guitar, cello, double bass, voice, and more.
The Montclair performance will take place on Sunday, September 13, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. in Memorial Auditorium at Montclair State University. The event is co-sponsored by the Department of Global Cultural Studies.
Visit ZEFFY to purchase tickets
View the official flyer for this event here.
Hosted by: College of Humanities and Social Sciences (CHSS)
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12679147
Source: Montclair State University

item.title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays) — Sun Sep 20, 9:00 AM
item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).
**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one

item.title: Fall Symposium: Reclaiming the Narrative — Thu Oct 1, 9:00 AM — Westminster Hall
item.description:
In celebration of Archives Month, University Libraries will highlight how primary source materials can bring marginalized stories to the center of education, advocacy, and community engagement. Dr. Melissa Benbow Flowers, Scholar‑in‑Residence at Sprague Library (2025–2026), in collaboration with Bloomfield College, will host a symposium exploring how working‑class histories and undertold stories in New Jersey are researched, interpreted, and shared with the public. The program will bring together scholars, students, museum professionals, and public historians whose work focuses on labor, domestic work, immigration, race, and community change—particularly as these histories are communicated through museums, historic sites, archives, and public‑facing scholarship. Registration is free and open to students, faculty, staff, and members of the public—but limited! Registration closes September 18. Register Now
Hosted by: Sprague Library

item.title: Everything Book Club, "The Ministry of Time" by Kaliene Bradley, Session 2 — Thu Oct 8, 1:15 PM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
An instant New York Times bestseller. In the near future, a new government ministry is exploring time travel. Our heroine gets a highly paid job assisting and monitoring the time travel expat known as “1847” or Commander Graham Gore. As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.” This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.
"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . . A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . . with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

The Teach Yourself Mah Jongg provides a weekly opportunity for teaching yourself the basics of American Mah Jongg at your own pace.
The library will provide the book Beginner's Guide to American Mah Jongg by Elaine Sandberg, Mah Jongg card, a set and table! You can also boost your learning with a list of Mah Jongg resources available at the library.
After you know the basics of Mah Jongg, and would like to play the game with other Mah Jongg players, please register for the weekly Thursday or the weekly Saturday "Mah Jongg Meetup".
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Thursday Morning — Thu Oct 15, 11:00 AM — Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - Classroom
item.description:
PLEASE NOTE: You must sign up for EACH INDIVIDUAL SESSION. Signing up for one session does not register you for any following classes.
The Mah Jongg Meetup provides a weekly opportunity for players to continue practicing their established skills, sharpen their strategies, build confidence at the game table, and socialize with fellow Mah Jongg players!
The library will provide a set and table! NOTE: Attendees should already have an understanding of the Mah Jongg game. Attendees should bring their 2025 or 2026 National Mah Jongg League card to the meetup. Bringing an additional set is encouraged!
There is also "Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Monday Morning". If you are interested, please register here
If you prefer to play the game on the weekend, please register for the "Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Saturday Afternoon" by clicking here
If you're new to the game, and would like to teach yourself at your own pace, please register for the "Teach Yourself Mah Jongg" by clicking here.
